focus: PSK-SEC10-01 loopback CSRF and authentication closure
key lifecycle, protocol privacy, and artifact retention
summary: The loopback browser harness now requires same-origin POST JSON with exact Host/Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site, per-case in-memory CSRF token and Bearer auth, no cookies, and no CORS, with negative browser cases rejected before Coordinator. The log field is now a fresh random request_trace_id explicitly independent from decision_id and Registry TraceID. OpenVerified now precedes every receipt/DB/sidecar/key access path. No new security blocker was found in this read-only review.

round10_dispositions.evidence: §6 requires loopback-only binding, exact Host/Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin, POST JSON, in-memory per-case X-Pilot-CSRF and Bearer auth; prohibits cookie auth, GET/form, missing Origin, and CORS; token is excluded from URL/storage/log. Cross-origin/forged Host/missing token/wrong content type/GET E2E cases assert pre-Coordinator rejection and zero Planner/Registry calls.
§7 uses random per-request request_trace_id and explicitly defines it as independent, non-derivable, and non-reusable relative to decision_id and Registry TraceID.

control_dispositions.acl_before_db_and_receipt: specified for coordinator start, all receipt paths including hits, and each actual file open; failures stop before query/planner
control_dispositions.per_case_key_and_delivery: fresh independent unique 256-bit OS-CSPRNG key; protected same-case restart recovery and inherited handle/pipe delivery specified
control_dispositions.same_account_threat_boundary: explicitly excluded; receipt-first limited to structural consistency within trusted local-account boundary
control_dispositions.degraded_sidecar_receipt_recovery: authorized replay, case quarantine across restart, and fail-closed unavailable receipt behavior specified
control_dispositions.artifact_retention_cleanup: 24-hour terminal failure, 7-day pending/degraded, supervisor-only, grouped deletion and persistent cleanup quarantine specified
control_dispositions.protocol_privacy: request trace is distinct from decision/Registry trace; raw sensitive identifiers/content and tokens excluded from ordinary logs

limitations: No tests or runtime validation were run.
No browser request checks, ACL/key checks, build artifacts, database, or recovery flow were inspected at runtime.
Approval is limited to the written isolated test-only security design; it does not establish implementation correctness, production readiness, or classroom readiness.
